writeup: TIC 355921200 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.874048 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 1.92 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal carries a detection significance of 274.8 in the BLS periodogram, with pixel-level difference imaging confirming a peak signal-to-noise of 10.4, though the centroid offset of 4.1 arcseconds from the target warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, marking it as previously unknown. One open question remains: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true period may differ from initial measurements, though timing data support the corrected period reported here.
